A.depoimento: Our armies march on Santarem and Evora! By striking fast, we claim these vital lands for the crown and deny them to the enemy. The king's wrath is swift and unstoppable!
A.plano: Send mixed forces to capture Santarem and Evora simultaneously. Build 2 spearmen in Lisboa to maintain a defensive garrison and prepare for the next wave of expansion.

B.depoimento: The armies marched to capture the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona. In the capital, two new spearmans were forged. The expansion of our kingdom starts with these key victories!
B.plano: Capture Tarragona and Girona to expand territory and resource production. Build 2 spearman in Barcelona to maintain troop count. Consolidate new villages next turn before further expansion.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies captured Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro, securing our western flank. In Lisboa, we built a knight and sent spearmen to reinforce Santarem. We now turn our attention to the north and south, preparing to push into the heart of the peninsula.
A.plano: Next turn, assess the outcomes of the attacks. Build more troops in Lisboa (likely another knight) and plan the next attacks. Send troops from Coimbra to Porto, and from Badajoz or Faro to Sevilha. Keep an eye on the enemy capital.

B.depoimento: I launch a double strike against the neutral villages of Zaragoza and Huesca, sending the full garrisons of Tarragona and Girona. Simultaneously, I dispatch reinforcements from Barcelona to secure my new territories. In the capital, the forges produce two fresh spearmen to replenish my ranks. This bold move will expand my domain and bring me closer to victory.
B.plano: Next turn, focus on building troops in the newly captured Zaragoza and Huesca to establish defenses. Use the resources from all villages to expand the army. Prepare to attack Castellon from Tarragona and explore the road network to locate the enemy capital and other villages. Continue building spearmen in Barcelona to maintain population.

A.depoimento: This turn, we focus on consolidation and reinforcement. We move our northern spearman to Coimbra and our southern archers and knights to Badajoz and Faro, creating two powerful strike forces. We also build additional spearman, archers, and a knight to strengthen our villages for the upcoming assaults on the neutral territories.
A.plano: Move troops to Coimbra and Badajoz/Faro to prepare for the next turn's attacks. Build spearman in Coimbra, Santarem, Evora; archers in Badajoz, Faro; knight in Lisboa. Next turn, attack Porto with the gathered spearman and Sevilha with archers.

B.depoimento: I am launching a three-pronged attack to secure Madrid, Pamplona, and Castellon. My armies in Zaragoza, Huesca, and Tarragona are marching to these neutral villages. Simultaneously, I am rebuilding my forces in Barcelona, Girona, Huesca, Zaragoza, and Tarragona to ensure my empire remains strong.
B.plano: Capture Madrid, Pamplona, and Castellon this turn to expand to 8 villages. Rebuild troops in my core villages to prepare for the next phase of expansion. Focus on the central Spanish plains to secure resources.

A.depoimento: Our armies struck at Sevilha, shattering the neutral garrison with archers and knight. Coimbra is being reinforced for the push on Porto. The western flank is secure and growing.
A.plano: Next turn, attack Porto from Coimbra with the reinforced spearman (leave a small guard). After capturing Sevilha, send troops to explore Cordoba. Reinforce Badajoz with Faro's troops. Watch for enemy movements.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered the assault on Salamanca with Madrid's garrison, leveraging the spearman-knight counter to secure a vital western foothold. I am also reinforcing Madrid and Pamplona to consolidate our expanding borders, while focusing our economy on producing knights for the push toward Lisboa.
B.plano: Conquer Salamanca with Madrid's troops to open the western route to the enemy capital. Reinforce Madrid with 1 spearman from Zaragoza for the next attack on Toledo. Reinforce Pamplona with 1 spearman from Zaragoza after its conquest. Build knights in core villages to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: Sevilha is mine and Porto falls this turn after a bloody spear fight. I'm rushing reinforcements to Coimbra and Badajoz to shield the borders while the spearman tide rolls north. The enemy at Salamanca hasn't moved, but I won't give them an opening.
A.plano: Attack Porto from Coimbra with 9 spearman (leave 3 for defense — tie vs Salamanca's 7 attack holds). Santarem's 3 spearman + 2 knight reinforce Coimbra for next turn. Sevilha's archer+knight and Faro's 3 spearman reinforce Badajoz. Build 2 spearman in every village that can afford it. Watch Salamanca — do not attack it yet.

B.depoimento: This turn, we focused on building up our forces. We built knights in Barcelona, Zaragoza, and Huesca, archers in Tarragona, Girona, and Castellon, and spearman in Madrid. We sent a knight from Zaragoza to Madrid to prepare for an attack on Toledo. Our goal is to conquer Toledo next turn to expand our territory.
B.plano: We are building troops in all our villages to strengthen our army. We sent a knight from Zaragoza to Madrid to reinforce it for an attack on Toledo next turn. Madrid will have 3 spearman and 1 knight, which should be enough to conquer Toledo. After taking Toledo, we will plan further attacks on Porto and other neutral villages. We must not forget to attack Toledo from Madrid next turn.

A.depoimento: The great offensive begins on three fronts! Coimbra's spearmen and knights assault Salamanca, Badajoz's spear horde marches on Toledo, and swift knights ride south to Sevilha to set up Cordoba's fall. Every village builds troops — the tide is turning!
A.plano: Coimbra sends 6 spearman + 2 knight to Salamanca (attack 14 vs defense 8, easy win, keep 4 spearman for defense). Badajoz sends 7 spearman to Toledo (counter bonus 1.5x: 10.5 > 10 defense, victory). Badajoz also sends 2 knights to Sevilha — they arrive next turn and can take Cordoba with 2 knights (counter bonus: 12 > 10). Build 2 spearman everywhere affordable. Watch for enemy counter-movements on Coimbra and Badajoz.

B.depoimento: This turn, our armies strike on two fronts. From Madrid, our spearman and knight force marches on Toledo, leveraging the spearman's counter against their knights. From Castellon, our archer and knight assault Valencia, exploiting the archer's advantage against their spearmen. We are also building reinforcements across our realm to ensure our victory is sustained.
B.plano: We are attacking Toledo from Madrid with 3 spearman and 1 knight, and Valencia from Castellon with 1 archer and 1 knight. Both attacks should succeed due to counter bonuses. We are building troops in all villages to replenish our forces and prepare for further expansion next turn. After taking Toledo and Valencia, we will have 11 villages. We need to continue expanding towards the enemy territories and secure our borders.

A.depoimento: Reinforced Toledo with a knight, archers, and spearman from Badajoz to repel the enemy assault. Sent spearman from Santarem to strengthen Coimbra and Badajoz, and from Lisboa to Santarem. Built 2 spearman in all possible villages. The attack on Salamanca is underway.
A.plano: Next turn: check Salamanca and Toledo battle results. If Salamanca taken, send reinforcements there and attack Madrid. If Toledo holds, consider attacking Madrid from Toledo. Continue building. Watch for enemy attacks on Coimbra, Porto, Badajoz.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies strike at Madrid and Cordoba. The king's knights take Cordoba while spearman assault Madrid. We reinforce our borders and build for the coming campaign. Victory is within reach.
A.plano: Next turn: check results of Madrid and Cordoba attacks. If Madrid taken, send reinforcements from Toledo to hold it, and consider attacking Burgos. If Cordoba taken, build troops there. Continue building archers in Coimbra, Porto, Badajoz. Watch for enemy attacks on Coimbra, Porto, Badajoz, Toledo. Consider sending more archers to Coimbra to prepare for Salamanca attack.

B.depoimento: We launch a coordinated assault on the three neutral villages: Burgos, Teruel, and Murcia. Our knights from Pamplona and Zaragoza, along with the archers from Valencia, are sent to capture these key settlements and expand our territory. Meanwhile, our other villages work diligently to produce more troops to secure our borders and prepare for the upcoming campaigns.
B.plano: Capture the three neutral villages: Burgos, Teruel, and Murcia to boost our economy and troop production. Use Pamplona's knights for Burgos, Zaragoza's knights for Teruel, and Valencia's archers for Murcia. Build troops in all other villages to reinforce our garrisons and prepare for the next phase of the campaign against the enemy villages.

A.depoimento: King A orders knights to be built in every capable village, strengthening his army for the campaigns ahead. Troops from Toledo strike at the neutral territory of Teruel, while reinforcements pour into the western borders to prepare for an assault on Salamanca. The expansion eastward begins in earnest.
A.plano: Next turn: check results of Teruel and Madrid battles. If Teruel captured, send troops to hold it and start building there. If Madrid garrison weakened, send a strong force from Toledo (including newly built knights) to take it. Continue moving troops from interior to western borders. Build archers in Cordoba once it has resources. Watch for enemy attacks on Toledo and Porto; reinforce if needed.

B.depoimento: This turn we are fortifying our positions. We are sending a large force to Madrid to hold the line, and gathering armies at Zaragoza and Valencia to strike the neutral villages next turn. Our builds are focused on rebuilding our knight corps and archers for the upcoming assaults.
B.plano: Reinforce Madrid with 9 knights and 3 archers to defend against the incoming enemy army. Send 3 knights to Zaragoza to prepare for attack on Teruel. Send 1 archer and 2 knights to Valencia to prepare for attack on Murcia. Build troops in all villages to replenish forces. Next turn, capture the three neutral villages: Burgos, Teruel, and Murcia.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a massive multi-front offensive! My armies are marching on Burgos, Murcia, Teruel, and Porto simultaneously. By utilizing the counter triangle, I expect to sweep through these villages and significantly expand my territory. The enemy will struggle to defend against such a coordinated assault!
B.plano: Launch a coordinated offensive to capture Burgos, Murcia, Teruel, and Porto. Use the counter triangle effectively (archers against spearmen, knights against archers) to ensure victories. Build troops in all villages to replenish forces and prepare for the next wave of expansions towards Toledo and Badajoz.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched a double strike from Coimbra, sending a mixed force to Porto and a spearhead of spearmen to Salamanca. In the east, our knights in Teruel charged Valencia. Reinforcements from the interior rivers flowed to Coimbra and Badajoz, while Sevilha sent troops to Cordoba. Our builders worked tirelessly, forging knights and archers across the realm. The web of war tightens.
A.plano: We sent all from Coimbra to Porto and Salamanca, left 2s. Reinforcements from Lisboa and Santarem arrive turn 13. Teruel sent all to Valencia, build 2s for defense. Sevilha sent to Cordoba. Watch for enemy attacks on Coimbra and Teruel. Next turn, attack Salamanca with the 14s arriving turn 14. Also, send the Cordoba troops to Toledo and attack Murcia. Build in all villages as ordered.

B.depoimento: Our forces strike at the enemy's weak points, capturing Cordoba and Teruel while our interior sends reinforcements to the front. We build troops across our realm to sustain the offensive and defend our borders.
B.plano: Capture Cordoba and Teruel to reach 15 villages. Reinforce Murcia, Castellon, Porto, and Salamanca with troops from interior villages. Build archers and spearmen in all villages to replenish forces and prepare for future attacks on Toledo and Vigo. Hold borders strong against enemy counterattacks.

B.depoimento: I am launching a coordinated offensive on Valencia and Toledo to secure my borders and increase my village count. I am also reinforcing my western front at Salamanca to prepare for any enemy counterattacks.
B.plano: Launch a double offensive on Valencia and Toledo to expand my territory. Reinforce Castellon and Madrid before the attacks to ensure they have enough garrison. Defend Salamanca by sending reinforcements from Porto. Build troops across all villages to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: We are King A. This turn, we are reinforcing Toledo to meet the enemy army marching on our capital region, while sending a strong force from Coimbra to take Porto. Our interior villages are sending their troops to the front lines. We are building knights and spearmen to grow our army. We expect to capture Porto and hold Toledo, moving closer to our goal of 18 villages.
A.plano: This turn: send all Coimbra troops to Porto; send Badajoz and Cordoba reinforcements to Toledo; send troops from interior to reinforce Coimbra and Badajoz. Build knights and spearmen across realm. Watch the enemy army at Toledo; ensure we have enough to win. Next turn, prepare to attack Salamanca and Madrid.

B.depoimento: I am launching a massive triple offensive on Toledo, Cordoba, and Vigo this turn to expand my empire. My armies are marching to reinforce every border village, ensuring we have the strength to conquer more territory and secure the 18 villages needed for victory.
B.plano: Launch attacks on Toledo (already marching), Cordoba, and Vigo to expand my territory to 17 villages. Reinforce all border villages (Madrid, Teruel, Murcia, Porto, Zaragoza, Castellon, etc.) to prepare for the next offensive towards Coimbra and Sevilha. Build troops across all villages to maintain army strength and replace losses.

B.depoimento: I am building up my forces along the western and southern borders. Reinforcements are marching to Vigo and Murcia to launch coordinated attacks on Porto and Cordoba next turn. The doomed attack on Toledo is left to its fate; I will not waste more troops there.
B.plano: Focus on taking Cordoba and Porto to reach 16 villages. Reinforce Murcia and Vigo for attacks next turn. Build troops across all villages to maintain army strength. Ignore Toledo for now as it's too strong. Next turn, attack Cordoba from Murcia and Porto from Vigo.

A.depoimento: Our armies launched a major assault on Salamanca from Coimbra, aiming to break the enemy's western defenses. Reinforcements from across our empire rushed to support the attack and defend our borders. The war for dominance continues.
A.plano: We sent all of Coimbra's troops to attack Salamanca, expecting to capture it. Reinforcements from Porto and Badajoz are moving to Coimbra to maintain its defense. Interior villages are sending knights to Badajoz to build a strike force. Next turn, we will send troops to hold Salamanca and plan the attack on Madrid.

B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of knights across my realm to boost my army's strength and speed. I am sending reinforcements from Valencia to Murcia and from Burgos to Vigo. My main armies are marching to attack Cordoba and Porto, aiming to capture these villages and reach 16 holdings.
B.plano: After capturing Cordoba and Porto, we will have 16 villages. We need to find two more to win. I will send scouts to explore the unexplored regions and find enemy villages. I will continue building troops to maintain our military strength and prepare for further attacks. I will keep an eye on Badajoz and Coimbra but will not attack them until we have more troops.

A.depoimento: We launched a double strike this turn: our Coimbra garrison took Salamanca, while Toledo's army conquered Madrid. Badajoz sent reinforcements to both fronts to secure our gains. All villages produced troops to strengthen our defenses. The enemy capital is now within our reach as we push east.
A.plano: Salamanca is being taken by Coimbra troops. Madrid is being attacked by Toledo's full army. Badajoz is sending reinforcements to both Salamanca and Toledo. We built troops in all villages to maintain garrisons. Next turn, we will assess the losses and plan the attacks on Porto and Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: King B's forces are on the move! We are launching a pincer attack on Sevilha and Coimbra, sending our finest troops to capture these key enemy villages. If we succeed, we will finally reach the 18-village threshold needed for victory. We are also reinforcing our borders to protect our gains while our villages work tirelessly to build a new generation of knights and archers.
B.plano: We are launching a double attack this turn: Cordoba to Sevilha and Porto to Coimbra. If both succeed, we will reach 18 villages and be on the path to victory. We are reinforcing Cordoba with Murcia's troops, Porto with Vigo's troops, and Salamanca with Madrid's troops to defend against enemy counter-attacks. We are building extensively in all our villages to grow our army for the next turns.

B.depoimento: This turn, we ordered a major offensive on two fronts. From Porto, we sent a large force to attack Coimbra, while Cordoba's troops assault Sevilha. Simultaneously, we reinforced our vulnerable border villages: Zaragoza sent troops to Madrid, and we bolstered Salamanca with archers from Porto and Madrid. Our villages are building at full capacity to replenish our ranks. We hope to capture two enemy villages and reach the 18-victory threshold.
B.plano: We are launching a double attack on Coimbra and Sevilha this turn, aiming to capture both and reach 18 villages. We are sending all available troops from Porto to Coimbra and from Cordoba to Sevilha. We are reinforcing Madrid from Zaragoza and Salamanca from Porto and Madrid to defend against enemy attacks. We are building extensively in all villages to grow our army for the next turns. Next turn, we will need to send reinforcements to the captured villages to hold them and repel enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: I have launched a three-pronged attack: Toledo on Cordoba, Madrid on Burgos, and Badajoz on Sevilha. Reinforcements are moving to Coimbra and Faro to secure the borders. My armies should overwhelm the enemy garrisons and expand my kingdom.
A.plano: Next turn: check if any of our villages were attacked. If Coimbra is safe, attack Porto from Coimbra. Also, consider attacking Zaragoza from Madrid or from the new Burgos. Build more knights and archers in all villages. Watch for enemy movements on the eastern front.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies struck at Cordoba, Porto, and Sevilha, expanding our territory. We have also sent reinforcements to secure Burgos and strengthen Coimbra and Badajoz. Our forces are ready to push further east next turn.
A.plano: Next turn: reinforce newly captured Cordoba, Porto, and Sevilha. Attack Vigo from Burgos. Attack Zaragoza from Madrid if possible. Build more knights and archers. Watch for enemy counterattacks.

B.depoimento: King B orders the construction of archers along the southern and eastern borders to counter the enemy's spear-heavy garrisons. The army of Pamplona marches to conquer the weakly defended Burgos, while Salamanca's archers strike at Madrid. Reinforcements are sent to Teruel and Zaragoza to prepare for the next wave of assaults.
B.plano: We are focusing on conquering Burgos this turn using Pamplona's army, which counters the enemy's archers. We are also attacking Madrid from Salamanca with a counter-typed army of archers. We are building archers in border villages (Zaragoza, Teruel, Cordoba, Sevilha, Salamanca) and knights in interior villages to prepare for future attacks. We are reinforcing Teruel and Zaragoza to launch double attacks on Toledo and Madrid next turn.

A.depoimento: I am launching a massive coordinated strike on four fronts! My knights from Coimbra storm Porto, my Madrid forces crush Burgos, Toledo's army overwhelms Cordoba, and Badajoz's spearmen sweep into Salamanca. The enemy's thin garrisons stand no chance against my combined arms. Sevilha's knights march to reinforce Badajoz for the next wave. All my villages are building knights at full capacity — the tide is turning.
A.plano: Four coordinated attacks on the enemy's weakest villages. Coimbra takes Porto, Madrid takes Burgos, Toledo takes Cordoba, Badajoz takes Salamanha. Sevilha reinforces Badajoz. All western villages build knights for next turn's push. Check results of all four battles next turn and pivot to Vigo/Zaragoza/Murcia.

B.depoimento: We are striking on all fronts this turn! Our armies from Zaragoza, Teruel, and Cordoba are marching to conquer Madrid, Toledo, and Sevilha respectively, which will bring us to the 18-village victory threshold. Meanwhile, we are reinforcing Porto from Vigo to prepare for the next push into Coimbra, and our villages are busy building troops to replenish our ranks.
B.plano: We are launching a triple attack this turn to conquer Madrid (from Zaragoza), Toledo (from Teruel), and Sevilha (from Cordoba) to reach the 18-village threshold. We are also reinforcing Porto from Vigo to prepare for an attack on Coimbra next turn. We are building troops across all our villages to replenish losses and prepare for the next turn's defense and expansion.

B.depoimento: I ordered a massive coordinated assault along the enemy's western borders. From Porto, Madrid, and Toledo, I marched strong mixed armies to capture Coimbra, Burgos, and Cordoba. In each of these key cities, I also ordered the construction of spearman to ensure our newly conquered territories and home cities remain well-defended.
B.plano: Launch a simultaneous three-pronged attack on Coimbra, Burgos, and Cordoba from Porto, Madrid, and Toledo respectively to conquer three enemy villages and reach the 18-village threshold for victory. Build spearman in the sending villages to replenish garrisons and maintain defenses. Monitor the enemy capital and remaining villages for next turn.

A.depoimento: Our forces captured Sevilha, adding to our domain. We are fortifying our borders and building up our armies for the next push. The enemy will find us stronger next turn.
A.plano: We did not attack Porto this turn to keep Salamanca strong against Coimbra. We attacked Sevilha from Faro with a knight-led force, leaving a defense in Faro. We sent all troops from Lisboa to Santarem and from Evora to Faro to reinforce. We built troops in all villages to prepare for next turn's attacks. We will attack Coimbra from Santarem and Porto from Salamanca next turn.

B.depoimento: Turn 25: I secure my western borders by reinforcing Sevilha, Toledo, and Madrid while launching a targeted strike on Salamanca. Leaving spearmen in Madrid ensures the city holds if the enemy counterattacks. I build spearman across the empire to recover from recent losses and prepare for the next turn. The enemy may take Porto, but Salamanca will fall to my archers and knights.
B.plano: Reinforce all vulnerable border villages to prevent enemy attacks. Send Cordoba to Sevilha, Teruel to Toledo, and Burgos to Madrid to plug defensive gaps. Attack Salamanca with archers and knights from Madrid, leaving spearmen behind to defend the city. Build spearman in all villages to replenish losses and grow the army. Coimbra should hold against Santarem due to the spearman counter bonus. Porto may fall if Salamanca attacks, but taking Salamanca will offset the loss.

A.depoimento: We strike at Porto from Badajoz with an archer-led force that turns the enemy's own spearmen against them. Our interior villages empty their garrisons to feed the front — Lisboa's troops rush to Santarem, Evora's knights to Faro. We build knights across every village, betting on quality and timing. The Sevilha march is a sacrifice we accept; Porto is the prize worth the steel.
A.plano: Attack Porto from Badajoz with 3 archers + 3 knights: archer majority counters Porto's spearmen (21 effective vs 18 defense). Send all Lisboa troops to Santarem and all Evora knights to Faro for reinforcement. Do NOT attack Coimbra yet — too costly at current strength. The Faro army marching to Sevilha will be destroyed next turn; accept that loss. After Porto is captured, gather forces at Salamanca for the next push.
